Learn how to draw circles and arcs with a compass.

In template mode, each level contains a template to replicate or to get inspiration from. In free mode, you can draw freely and adjust the canvas size and grid spacing as you want from the compass settings menu.
Move the compass by dragging the leg without the pen.
Move the pen by dragging the other leg or the circle around the pen tip.
Rotate and draw by dragging the pen with the left mouse button.
Rotate without drawing by dragging the compass hinge, or by dragging the pen with the right mouse button.
The snap to grid setting can be temporarily inverted by pressing the Control key.
Each level in template mode presents a template to replicate or to get inspiration from.
Each template is divided into steps which can be scrolled through using the arrows.
Each step shows where to place the tip of the compass and the circle or arc to be drawn.
You can change the position of the template by clicking on its corners.
Ctrl: invert snap to grid while it is pressed

Make beautiful drawings by rolling the gear in the cogwheel with the chosen pen. Select a wheel size, a gear size, pen's settings and color from the popup panels, and press the play button to roll the gear. On the first level, only some specific wheel and gear size combinations are available to get started. On the second level, all size combinations are available to give more creative freedom. You can use the file menu to save your image, open a previously saved image, or create a new image with selected background color. Saving an image will save it in an SVG file (vector format), along with a PNG file (pixel format). Only the SVG file can be opened again from the activity.

Bisons live on the plains of North America and were hunted by the Native Americans for food. However, their near-extinction is due to the fact that the colonizers massacred them for sport and to clear land, rather than to hunting by indigenous peoples.

Read the instructions that give you the range of the number to find. Enter a number in the top right entry box, and press the OK button to validate it. You will be told if your number is higher or lower than the one to find. Then try again until you find the correct answer. The distance between the helicopter and the right side of the screen represents how far you are from the number to find. If the helicopter is above or under the vertical center of the screen, it means your number is higher or lower than the number to find.

Remove all the pieces in the correct order until only one remains.

To move a piece, make it jump another one in an orthogonal direction, to a hole two positions away. The jumped piece is removed from the board. You can click on a movable piece and then on its destination, or drag and drop it to its destination. The game is over when no more piece can be moved, and is won if only one piece remains. If the option to use the default starting hole is not selected, you need to choose the first piece to remove by clicking on it. You can use the undo button to undo your last move, and the redo button to redo it.
Learn about special polygons and draw them in a grid.

Click on the grid to place points corresponding to the ends of the polygon's lines. As long as the shape is not closed, the last point is of a different color to indicate that it will be connected to the next point added. After placing at least 3 points, you can close the shape by clicking on the first or the last point. When the shape is closed, you can not add new points. You can move a point by dragging it, or delete it with a double-click. You can restart the shape by clicking on the reload button. When the shape is correct, press the OK button to validate your answer.
Arrows: move the keyboard cursor in the grid, and if a point is selected move it
Enter: create a point at the cursor position, or validate your answer when the shape is closed
Space: select or deselect the point at the cursor position
A polygon is a closed shape made of at least 3 connected lines.
To draw a polygon, click on the grid to place the ends of the polygon's lines.
After placing at least 3 points, you can close the shape by clicking on the first or the last point.
The points should not be all aligned.
A triangle is a polygon with 3 sides.
A right triangle is a triangle in which two sides are perpendicular, forming a right angle (90 degrees).
An isosceles triangle is a triangle with two sides of equal length and two angles of equal measure.
A quadrilateral is a four-sided polygon, having 4 sides and 4 corners.
A rectangle is a quadrilateral with 4 right angles.
A square is a rectangle with 4 sides of equal length.
A parallelogram is a quadrilateral with opposite sides of equal length and opposite angles of equal measure.
Draw a parallelogram which is not a rectangle.
A rhombus is a parallelogram with four sides of equal length.
Draw a rhombus which is not a square.
